focus.title: 美国拟对东南亚四国光伏产品加征反倾销税，中国组件企业面临转口合规新考验
focus.summary: 美国商务部初步裁定，来自泰国、越南、马来西亚、柬埔寨的晶体硅光伏电池及组件存在倾销行为，拟征收17%至271%不等的反倾销税，并将追溯适用。此举将直接冲击中国企业在东南亚的转口产能布局。相关企业需在终裁前完成供应链合规审查，评估原产地规则及反规避风险，调整出口路径，并考虑通过美国建厂或技术授权等方式重构海外产能。
focus.title_en: US Preliminary AD Duties on Solar Imports from Four Southeast Asian Countries to Reshape Chinese Firms' Transshipment Strategies
focus.summary_en: The US Department of Commerce has preliminarily determined that crystalline silicon photovoltaic cells and modules from Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, and Cambodia were sold at less than fair value, proposing anti-dumping duties ranging from 17% to 271%, with retroactive application. This move directly impacts Chinese companies' transshipment production bases in Southeast Asia. Affected firms should conduct supply chain compliance reviews before the final determination, assess rules of origin and anti-circumvention risks, adjust export routes, and consider restructuring overseas capacity through US-based manufacturing or technology licensing.

case.title: 新加坡国际仲裁中心裁决获中国法院承认与执行，仲裁协议效力审查成关键
case.summary: 某中国企业与新加坡公司因货物买卖合同纠纷，在新加坡国际仲裁中心（SIAC）进行仲裁。裁决作出后，新加坡公司向中国法院申请承认与执行。中国法院依据《纽约公约》审查后，认定双方仲裁协议有效，裁决不违反中国公共政策，遂裁定承认与执行。该案提示，跨境合同中仲裁条款的明确性、独立性及争议事项的可仲裁性，是裁决能否在中国获得执行的关键；企业应确保仲裁条款符合中国法律及《纽约公约》要求。
case.title_en: Chinese Court Recognizes and Enforces SIAC Award, Highlighting Key Role of Arbitration Agreement Validity
case.summary_en: In a dispute over a goods sale contract between a Chinese enterprise and a Singapore company, arbitration was conducted at the Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC). After the award was rendered, the Singapore company sought recognition and enforcement in Chinese courts. The Chinese court, reviewing under the New York Convention, found the arbitration agreement valid and the award not contrary to Chinese public policy, thus granting recognition and enforcement. This case underscores that the clarity, independence, and arbitrability of the arbitration clause in cross-border contracts are crucial for enforcement in China; enterprises should ensure arbitration clauses comply with Chinese law and the New York Convention.

policy.title: 粤港澳大湾区跨境数据流动新规落地，企业数据出境安全评估流程简化
policy.summary: 国家网信办联合粤港澳三地发布大湾区数据跨境流动便利化措施，对符合条件的一般个人信息和重要数据出境实行负面清单管理，简化安全评估程序，并设立绿色通道。此举旨在促进大湾区科研、金融、医疗等领域数据融合。相关企业应尽快梳理数据资产，对照负面清单判断是否适用便利化措施，完善数据分类分级及合规制度，并利用新规提升跨境业务效率。
policy.source: 来源：国家互联网信息办公室 · 2026.08.01
policy.title_en: New GBA Cross-Border Data Flow Rules Simplify Security Assessment for Enterprises
policy.summary_en: The Cyberspace Administration of China, together with Guangdong, Hong Kong, and Macau authorities, has issued facilitation measures for cross-border data flows in the Greater Bay Area, adopting negative list management for eligible general personal information and important data outbound transfers, simplifying security assessment procedures, and establishing a green channel. This aims to promote data integration in research, finance, healthcare, and other sectors. Enterprises should promptly map their data assets, check against the negative list to determine eligibility, improve data classification and compliance systems, and leverage the new rules to enhance cross-border business efficiency.

analysis.title: 美国《反外国勒索法》生效在即，中国企业需警惕跨境合规风险
analysis.summary: 秦林蒿律师研判：美国《反外国勒索法》（FEPA）即将生效，旨在打击外国政府通过贸易限制、关税等手段强迫美国企业从事特定行为。中国企业若参与此类行为，可能面临美国民事索赔。建议企业：一是全面审查对美业务中的政府压力来源，避免被动卷入；二是建立内部合规培训，确保员工理解FEPA风险；三是在合同中加入反腐败与合规条款，并寻求专业法律意见。
analysis.title_en: Attorney Qin's view: US Anti-Foreign Extortion Act Imminent, Chinese Enterprises Should Prepare for Compliance Risks
analysis.summary_en: Attorney Qin's view: The US Foreign Extortion Prevention Act (FEPA) is about to take effect, targeting foreign governments that use trade restrictions, tariffs, or other means to coerce US companies into specific actions. Chinese enterprises involved in such practices may face civil claims in the US. It is recommended that companies: first, thoroughly review sources of government pressure in US-related business to avoid passive involvement; second, establish internal compliance training to ensure employees understand FEPA risks; third, include anti-corruption and compliance clauses in contracts, and seek professional legal advice.
